mission.title: Install and Configure Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
mission.description: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is a managed Kubernetes service that simplifies the deployment, management, and operations of Kubernetes clusters in Azure. It is ideal for users who want to leverage Kubernetes without the overhead of managing the underlying infrastructure. Key trade-offs include reliance on Azure's ecosystem and potential costs associated with resource usage.

steps.title: Install Azure CLI
steps.description:
This step installs the Azure CLI, which is required to interact with Azure services.

```bash

curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash

```

> For Debian-based systems.

steps.title: Create AKS Cluster
steps.description:
This command creates a new AKS cluster with the specified Kubernetes version, node count, and region.

```bash

az aks create --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --node-count 3 --kubernetes-version 1.31 --location eastus

```

> Replace 'myResourceGroup' and 'myAKSCluster' with your desired names.
commands: az aks create --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --node-count 3 --kubernetes-version 1.31 --location eastus

steps.title: Configure kubectl
steps.description:
This command configures kubectl to use the newly created AKS cluster.

```bash

az aks get-credentials --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster

```

> This merges the AKS cluster credentials into your kubeconfig.

steps.title: Verify Cluster Nodes
steps.description:
This command checks the status of the nodes in the AKS cluster to ensure they are running.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> You should see the nodes in 'Ready' status.

steps.title: Post-Install Configuration
steps.description:
This step sets up monitoring and autoscaling for your AKS cluster.

```bash

az aks enable-addons --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --addons monitoring

az aks update --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --enable-cluster-autoscaler --min-count 1 --max-count 5

```

> Enables monitoring with Azure Monitor.
> Enables cluster autoscaler.
commands: az aks enable-addons --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --addons monitoring

uninstall.title: Delete AKS Cluster
uninstall.description:
This command deletes the AKS cluster and all associated resources. Be aware that this will result in data loss and orphaned resources such as load balancers and persistent volumes.

```bash

az aks delete --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --yes --no-wait

```

uninstall.title: Remove Resource Group
uninstall.description:
This command removes the resource group, which will delete all resources within it.

```bash

az group delete --name myResourceGroup --yes --no-wait

```

upgrade.title: Upgrade AKS Cluster
upgrade.description:
Before upgrading, ensure you back up your workloads and configurations. This command upgrades the AKS cluster to the specified version.

```bash

az aks upgrade --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --kubernetes-version 1.31

```

> Replace with your desired version.

upgrade.title: Verify Upgrade
upgrade.description:
After the upgrade, verify that the nodes are running the new version.

```bash

kubectl get nodes

```

> Check that nodes are in 'Ready' status and running the new version.

upgrade.title: Post-Upgrade Configuration
upgrade.description:
Reapply any configurations or monitoring settings that may have been reset during the upgrade.

```bash

az aks enable-addons --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --addons monitoring

```

> Re-enable monitoring if needed.
commands: az aks enable-addons --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster --addons monitoring

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to create the AKS cluster'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur due to insufficient permissions or quota limits in your Azure subscription.

**Fix:**
Check your Azure subscription permissions and ensure you have enough quota for the requested resources.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'kubectl get nodes' returns 'No resources found'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the AKS cluster may not be properly configured or the credentials are not set.

**Fix:**
Run 'az aks get-credentials --resource-group myResourceGroup --name myAKSCluster' to configure kubectl.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Insufficient CPU resources available'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This indicates that the requested node count exceeds the available resources in the selected region.

**Fix:**
Reduce the node count or select a different region with more available resources.

troubleshooting.title: Error: 'Failed to enable monitoring'
troubleshooting.description:
**Cause:** This may occur if the Azure Monitor service is not available in your region.

**Fix:**
Check the Azure Monitor availability in your region or try enabling it after the cluster is created.
